Called shots

Call
Declaration

Official rules: each game's own (8-ball WPA, 10-ball and straight pool call every shot; 9-ball and rotation none). A missed call is not a foul: the turn ends.

Aim guide

Full runs both balls' paths out; short shows the ghost ball and a stub; off draws nothing.

Auto aim

Auto aim starts each turn pointed at the ball to play next. The cut is up to you.

Layout

Hand
Power bar

Left-handed mirrors the controls: the strip under the table runs the other way, and on its side the column stands left of the table. At the edge puts the power bar under your thumb, at the end of the strip or the foot of the column.

Keyboard: the arrows aim, Alt or Ctrl for a hair. Tab to the power bar, then up and down set its mark. Accessibility can let Space drive the bar.

Cloth

The cloth applies to every game (blue is carom's classic).

Look

Camera

Follow moves in a little on the action while the balls roll, and close on replays. Aiming always shows the whole table.

Replays

Offer puts a Replay pill over the table after a shot. Never keeps the table clear after every shot.

Motion

On: no sliding sheets, swings or pulses, whatever the system says. Off: follows the system setting.

Sound

Table sounds are the balls, cushions, cue and pockets; the master volume is everything, the game's little cues too. felt has no music or ambience.

Haptics

A tick for a hard contact, two for a pot, three for a win.

Seeing the table

Ball marks put an upright badge on every ball: solids light with a dark number, stripes dark with a light one, snooker's colours their value, carom's yellow Y and red R, bumper pool's reds R. Tell them apart without colour.

Text size

Menus, sheets, banners and the call bar grow; the table keeps its size.

Keyboard

For keyboard and switch players. Tab to the power bar, set its mark with up and down, then Space or Enter: the bar pulls to the mark and lets go, as a finger would. Any other key stops it. Off, no key ever shoots.

felt Pool, snooker and carom in one page. Offline, no account, nothing leaves the device.

How to play

  • Aim

    Point at the cloth or click a spot. Drag to swing the cue round the ball.

  • Fine-tune

    ← → nudge the aim, with Shift for big steps and Alt for tiny ones. The ridged wheel works too.

  • Shoot

    Pull along the power bar and let go. The further you pull, the harder the hit.

  • Spin

    Move the blue tip on the cue ball: high for follow, low for draw. Double click it or press R to centre. Right click it, or press Page Up and Page Down on it, to raise the cue: with side spin a raised cue curves the ball (a swerve low, a masse high).

  • Ball in hand

    Drag the cue ball to place it. Or press M, move it with the arrows, and press M again.

  • Pause

    Press Esc or the pause button. Esc also closes this page.

  • Aim

    Drag anywhere on the table to swing the cue. Or tap where the cue ball should go.

  • Fine-tune

    Roll the ridged wheel beside the power bar for the last hair.

  • Shoot

    Pull along the power bar and let go. The further you pull, the harder the hit.

  • Spin

    Move the blue tip on the cue ball: high for follow, low for draw. Double tap it to centre. Hold it to raise the cue: with side spin a raised cue curves the ball (a swerve low, a masse high).

  • Ball in hand

    Drag the cue ball to place it, as often as you like. Only the shot locks it in.

  • Pause

    Tap the pause button. The game waits.

Fine print

  • Only the power bar shoots. No click on the table ever will, and no key unless Settings, Accessibility lets Space drive the bar.
  • Tab to the power bar: up and down set its mark, where the next pull starts from.
  • To cancel a shot, bring the pull back past the start or slide off the bar.
  • A fine-tuned aim holds until the mouse moves away or clicks. The aim never follows the pointer off the cloth.
  • Auto aim starts each turn on the ball to play and marks a pocket. The cut is up to you.
  • Drop the cue ball somewhere illegal and it goes back to the last good spot. Shift with the arrows moves it further.
  • Only the power bar shoots. The table only aims.
  • To cancel a shot, slide back to the start or off the bar.
  • Auto aim starts each turn on the ball to play and marks a pocket. The cut is up to you.
  • To move the cue ball, start the drag on or next to it. Drop it somewhere illegal and it goes back to the last good spot.
  • Break

    Ball in hand behind the head string.

  • Groups

    The table is open until the first legal pot. That player takes the group: solids (1 to 7) or stripes (9 to 15).

  • Your shot

    Hit one of yours first. Then pot a ball or send any ball to a rail.

  • Go again

    Pot one of yours, in any pocket, and you shoot again.

  • Fouls

    The wrong ball first, no rail, or the cue ball down. Your opponent gets ball in hand anywhere.

  • Win

    Clear your group, then pot the 8.

  • Lose

    Pot the 8 before your group is clear, or scratch while potting it.

Fine print

  • Once your group is gone, the 8 is the ball to hit first.
  • An 8 potted on the break is spotted and the breaker carries on.
  • Rack

    Nine balls in a diamond: the 1 in front, the 9 in the middle. Break from behind the head string.

  • Lowest first

    Always hit the lowest ball on the table first. Then pot a ball or hit a rail.

  • Any pot counts

    Whatever drops counts, so combinations and caroms are fine.

  • Fouls

    Your opponent gets ball in hand anywhere.

  • Three in a row

    Three fouls in a row lose the game. You are warned after two.

  • Win

    Pot the 9 on a legal shot, early or last.

Fine print

  • The warning after two fouls shows on the chip and in the pause menu.
  • The game

    Red against white, five balls each, round twelve posts. There is no cue ball: you strike your own.

  • Aim for the far cup

    Pot your balls in the cup at the far end. Never your own cup.

  • Marked ball first

    Your ball with the spot must drop before any other of yours.

  • Pick a ball

    Tap one of yours to strike it. Auto aim picks one, and a line, for you.

  • Opening

    Red, then white, shoot their marked ball. Whoever potted goes next (red if both). If neither did, the one nearer the far cup.

  • Go again

    Pot one of yours in the far cup and you shoot again.

  • Fouls

    Striking their ball, one of yours in your own cup, an unmarked ball before your marked one, potting theirs, or a ball off the table.

  • After a foul

    Your balls that dropped go back to your marked spot. Your opponent drops one of theirs in.

  • Win

    The first with all five down.

Fine print

  • A foul on white's opening shot gives red the table.
  • Potting your opponent's ball counts for them.
  • The ball they drop in is their marked one if it is still up, else the one furthest from their cup.
  • With a keyboard, B picks the ball to strike.
  • Choose the classic octagon or the rectangle when you start.
  • The game

    Three balls and no pockets on a 10 ft table. You only ever strike your own cue ball: white for player 1, yellow for player 2.

  • Score a point

    Your cue ball hits both other balls, and three cushions before the second one.

  • Counting cushions

    Any order. The same cushion twice counts twice, and cushions before the first ball count too.

  • Go again

    Score and you shoot again. Otherwise the turn passes.

  • Break

    Hit the red first.

  • Fouls

    A ball off the table, or not the red first on the break. No point, and the turn passes.

  • Win

    The first to the race: 5, 10 or 15 points, chosen when you start.

Fine print

  • In the one-cushion game, one cushion is enough.
  • The break: the red on the foot spot, your opponent's ball on the head spot, yours beside it on the head string.
  • A ball off the table goes back on its spot.
  • The full aim guide traces your cue ball through its first three cushions, a dot on each.
  • The game

    Fifteen reds and six colours. Pot a red, then a colour, then a red again.

  • Reds

    A red is 1 point. While reds remain, potted colours come back on their spots.

  • The ball on

    After a red, the first colour the cue ball hits is the one you are on.

  • Colours last

    With the reds gone, pot the colours in order.

    234567 Yellow 2, green 3, brown 4, blue 5, pink 6, black 7.
  • Break

    Place the cue ball anywhere in the D, the half circle on the baulk line. Hit a red first.

  • Fouls

    Missing every ball, hitting or potting a ball you are not on, or going in-off. Your opponent scores 4 to 7.

  • After a foul

    They play from where the cue ball stopped, or from the D after an in-off.

  • Win the frame

    Most points wins. You can concede from the pause menu.

Fine print

  • A foul is worth the ball on or the highest ball involved, whichever is more, from 4 up to 7.
  • With only the black left, the first score or foul ends the frame. If that leaves it level, the black is re-spotted and the other player plays it from the D.
  • The usual break clips the end red of the back row and brings the cue ball back to baulk.
  • The bar on the top rail shows the break, the ball on and the points left, and says when snookers are needed.
  • Choose one frame or best of three, and the 10 ft or 12 ft table, when you start.
  • Not in felt yet: the free ball and the miss rule.
  • Rack

    Ten balls in a triangle: the 1 in front, the 10 in the middle. Break from behind the head string.

  • Legal break

    Hit the 1 first, then pot a ball or drive four to the cushions.

  • Lowest first

    Always hit the lowest ball first. Then pot a ball or hit a rail.

  • Call it

    Every shot: tap the ball, then the pocket. Obvious shots too.

  • Push out

    The shot after the break may be a push out. Your opponent shoots it or hands it back.

  • Win

    Pot the 10 as a called shot.

Fine print

  • A 10 on the break, or one that drops early or uncalled, is spotted. No win.
  • A called ball that misses ends your turn. If an uncalled ball dropped, your opponent shoots or hands it back.
  • Declare a safety with the Safety chip: what drops stays down and your turn ends.
  • An illegal break: your opponent takes the table or has you break again.
  • Three fouls in a row lose. You are warned after two.
  • The house rule "obvious shots free" calls an obvious shot for you from your aim.
  • The game

    Fifteen balls, any ball first. Call ball and pocket: each one made is a point.

  • Break

    Call a ball and pocket it, or send two balls and the cue ball to the cushions.

  • Carry on

    Make your call and you shoot again. Other balls that drop with it count too.

  • Re-rack

    With one ball left the other fourteen are racked again. Break the rack open with the last one.

  • Fouls

    A point off. Your opponent plays from where the cue ball stopped.

  • Win

    The first to the race: 25, 50, 100 or 150, chosen when you start.

Fine print

  • Three fouls in a row cost 15 more, and the fouler breaks a full rack.
  • A breaking foul costs two; your opponent takes the table or has you break again.
  • A miss, or a safety, scores nothing: balls that dropped come back on the foot spot.
  • On a re-rack the last ball and the cue ball stay put unless they are in the rack. Then the ball goes to the head spot, the cue ball to your hand behind the line.
  • The pause menu shows each player's best run.
  • Rack

    Fifteen balls: the 1 in front, the 2 and 3 in the back corners, the 15 in the middle.

  • Lowest first

    Always hit the lowest ball first. Then pot a ball or hit a rail.

  • Score

    Every ball you pot on a legal shot scores its number.

  • Go again

    Pot a ball and you shoot again.

  • Fouls

    No score. Balls potted come back on the foot spot; your opponent gets ball in hand.

  • Win

    The first to 61 of the 120 points on the table.

Fine print

  • 60 all with the table clear: the player who potted the last ball wins (a felt house rule).
  • When

    Settings, Gameplay: off, 8-ball only, each game's official rules, or every shot. A career event sets its own.

  • Call

    Tap the ball, then the pocket. The table marks both until the shot.

  • Obvious shots

    Where the rules allow, your aim calls it for you: "Calling: 6 in corner". Tap the pill to change it.

  • Safety

    Tap Safety to play one. Your turn ends whatever drops.

  • Shoot

    The power bar shoots as always. With a call missing it says Call your shot and waits.

  • Missed call

    Not a foul: your turn ends. 14.1 spots what dropped; 10-ball lets your opponent choose.

Fine print

  • Ball, pocket and rails (custom): also call Bank, Kick or Combo. Strict (custom): and nothing else may drop.
  • Fouls are judged apart from the call: a made call on a scratch is still a foul.
  • The pause menu keeps your declarations, made and missed.
  • Practice

    No opponent and no fouls, always your shot. Undo takes back the last one.

  • Practice tools

    The tools button holds ball in hand and reset rack. On a free table it adds and removes balls.

  • Drills

    In Practice: a few shots each, scored out of 100 from where the balls really went. Bronze, silver and gold by score; a career's practice is played here too.

  • Trick shots

    One layout, one goal. Show me plays one way to make it.

  • Stars

    Three for a make on the first try, two within three tries, one for any make.

  • Daily shot

    One trick shot a day, the same for everyone. Your first try counts.

  • Streak

    Play on consecutive days and it grows. Miss a day and it starts again.

  • Career

    Your own player among 300 others: enter events from the calendar, climb twelve tiers, season after season.

  • Matches

    Played on the table, on the event's own rules and race. Leaving one before its end forfeits it.

Fine print

  • Retries on the daily shot are practice. They never change your streak.
